conformance.aspect_note: Deliverable aspect UNCHANGED (720x720 bundle standard). Only the SOURCE canvas was widened (608 -> 1000 px, +196 px per side) before the standard normalisation, so the subject sits slightly smaller in frame than the #389/#415 normalisations - the ring now fits instead of being clipped.

expansion.method: Geometry-guided angular texture transfer (deterministic, per-frame). The Dark Wave ring was fitted as an ellipse annulus from its surviving top/bottom arcs (peak fit: centre ~(303, 595), outer semi-axes a~414 / b~434, annulus inner ratio k~0.56, temporally median-smoothed). Each pixel of the new side bands is parametrised by ellipse angle and radial scale; its colour is sampled from the SAME frame at the same radial scale and an angle rotated -/+90 degrees onto the fully visible bottom arc, continuing the band's dark core, twin purple rims, glyph texture and halo across the old edge line. The annulus hole stays white. Background beyond the ring: edge-smear with exponential fade to white (the source field is white). A 10 px feather strip inside each old edge blends original into synthesis so the pattern does not break on the seam. No randomness and no cross-frame borrowing: frame N's extension is a pure function of frame N, so the bands cannot boil or flicker.

framing_verification.method: Per-frame content extent (any channel < 235), the same measure that failed both prior candidates, run on the expanded raw frames (1000x1280) and on the normalised 720x720 clip.
framing_verification.seam_verdict: PASS - owner-eye sheets (peak old-vs-expanded + four seam close-ups at the old edge lines) show the band's dark core, twin rims and glyph strokes continuous across both old edge lines at peak. Caveat, stated not hidden: the side-arc glyph texture is an angularly transferred copy of the same frame's bottom-arc texture (glyph shapes warp near the extreme tips); it is a continuation of the ring, not a recovery of pixels the generator never drew.
